subject: CloudLanes competitive readout & next technical tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@cloudlanes.com>; Priya Gupta <priya.gupta@cloudlanes.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: CloudLanes competitive readout & next technical tests

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next tests so we can produce an apples-to-apples TCO readout vs HyperscalerX and their managed inference endpoint. High level takeaways from our conversation:

- Primary buying criteria: predictable cost per inference at 95th percentile latency <= 120ms for 512-token requests, and ability to sustain bursts to 250 qps during peak windows.
- Main workloads: multi-turn chat with 512 tokens avg, and document extraction pipelines with single-turn 1k tokens.
- Security/procurement asks: SOC 2 report and data residency info (we noted Redwood Private options).

Proposed test matrix we can run (we suggest Redwood handles the runs if you approve):

1) Unit economics sweep
   - Baseline per-1M tokens cost for: batch size 1 / 8 / 32
   - Compare: Redwood hosted model (quantized variant) vs HyperscalerX managed endpoint (same model family)

2) Cache/batching sensitivity
   - KV-prefix cache hit scenarios: 0%, 50%, 90% (simulate replay of representative traces)
   - Measure: token cost, p50/p95 latency, end-to-end tail latency under 250 qps burst

3) Fallback routing test
   - Route 10% of traffic to lower-cost model variant during simulated capacity constraint and measure quality delta (automated BLEU/ROUGE + simple prompt set)

Deliverables we will share after the runs:
- Per-scenario cost sheet (per-1M tokens breakout)
- Latency/throughput matrix and recommended production config (batching, autoscale, cache settings)
- Short note describing reliability/fallback behavior and any tradeoffs

Attachments: CloudLanes_MutualActionPlan.xlsx (MVP timeline + owners), redwood-hyperscaler-cost-comparison-v1.pdf (example template).

As next steps: can you share a 30–60 minute representative trace (or sample NDJSON logs) and confirm who on procurement we should loop in for SOC2 / contract baseline? If you’re good with Redwood running the technical sweep, we can schedule a dedicated run window (need ~4 hours for full matrix).

Thanks — I’ll book a follow-up slot for early next week unless you prefer the run this week.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Priya Gupta <priya.gupta@cloudlanes.com>

Cc: Samir Shah <samir@cloudlanes.com>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2028 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudLanes competitive readout & next technical tests

Thanks Marissa — useful summary.

A few clarifications from our side before you run anything:

- We can provide a 2-hour trace covering both chat and document extract flows (will scrub PII). Expect to hand that off by end of day tomorrow.
- Procurement: loop in Nico (nico.procure@cloudlanes.com) for SOC2/contract discussion. He’ll want the SOC2 Type II and our DPA template answers.
- On metrics: p95 <=120ms is the target but we can accept p95 up to 200ms if per-1M cost delta is >20% lower (especially for document extract batch flows).

For the unit economics table please include: effective per-1M tokens cost, effective CPU/GPU cost attribution, and an example run-rate projection for 10M tokens/month.

We’re OK with Redwood running the sweep if you can host the runs in us-west and provide an anonymized result package we can share internally. Can you confirm the exact time requirement and whether the runs will consume any of our CloudLanes capacity (we’d prefer no impact on production).

—
Priya Gupta
Head of Product, CloudLanes
priya.gupta@cloudlanes.com

Looping in a concise test plan and what we’ll measure so everyone has expectations.

Plan (short):
- Run matrix in a staging environment in us-west (no impact on CloudLanes prod).
- Inputs: sample-log-trace.ndjson (will replay requests), 512/1024 token histograms.
- Variants: Redwood quantized-llama-48k (q4) and Redwood full-precision baseline; HyperscalerX-managed (same model family) as a reference.
- Metrics captured: token-cost, p50/p95 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, memory/KV cache hit ratio, throughput under controlled burst.

Scripts and benchmarks: we’ll run three passes per scenario (cold cache, warm cache, hot cache) and collect per-request cost attribution. I’ve attached a short runbook as code snippets in the Drive link (drive link above).

Est timing: 3.5–4.5 hours for full matrix (includes two warmup passes). We’ll produce the cost per-1M tokens table in the shared sheet and a one-page readout for execs.

Attachment references: sample-run-scripts.sh (in Drive), redwood-hyperscaler-cost-comparison-v1.pdf

Ben
